lessons.notes: Compared every paragraph with the complete VM checklist unit and current resize documentation. Avoided obsolete disk preview labels and unsupported universal VM disk counts.
Compared portal steps and prerequisites with the full exercise. No subscription deployment was performed; avoided hard-coded passwords and claims that public SSH is required for every VM.

Compared tool distinctions and CLI command syntax with the complete actual unit. Command uses existing lab group and authenticated intended subscription; it was not executed. Kept Automation general rather than recommending retired Automation Update Management.
Compared full availability unit with current VM reliability documentation. Avoided obsolete claims that a Standard Load Balancer is included free with VM tiers.

Compared full unit with current VM backup process, backup overview and MARS agent documentation. Retains Windows files/folders/system-state scope, agentless crash-consistent support and policy-controlled protection; no unlimited-transfer or retention promise.
Compared both sections with the entire maintenance unit and current VM reliability guidance. Distinguishes predictive live migration from unexpected host failure without promising zero interruption.
Compared set membership, tier separation and recreation requirements with complete unit and current availability-set documentation. No SLA or instance-count guarantee was added.
Compared all domain definitions and immutable update-domain count with full unit/current documentation. Worked example is conceptual, not a promise of a specific assignment pattern.
Compared zone versus region and zonal/zone-redundant distinctions with complete unit/current VM reliability documentation. Avoided implying that zonal placement automatically duplicates applications.
Compared complete vertical/horizontal unit and current resize process. Original workload comparison is conditional and does not assume all applications can scale out.
Compared complete scale-set unit and current orchestration-mode documentation. Preserves Flexible support for identical VMs and immutable mode; separates load balancing from redundancy.
Compared creation choices with complete unit and current spreading table. Avoided stale universal claim that fixed spreading always means five domains in every mode.
Compared sustained-demand and scheduled-capacity explanations with full unit and current autoscale/profile docs. No misleading schedule-as-webhook trigger or automatic vertical resizing claim.
Compared all settings with full configure-autoscale unit and current profile schema. Corrects default fallback semantics and keeps scale-in state assumptions explicit.
Compared complete plan-implementation unit and current hosting-plan docs. Uses dedicated-tier sharing and standard plan-wide behavior rather than claiming every tier has identical instance placement.
Compared full pricing unit with current hosting plans and automatic scaling docs. Avoided obsolete Isolated v1 recommendations and fixed slot/instance counts from training tables.
Compared full scaling unit and current plan/scale-up docs. Preserves dependency independence; qualifies plan-wide scaling and avoids zero-interruption guarantees.
Compared all sections against complete unit and current profile/automatic scaling documentation. Maintains per-app automatic scaling, Premium v4 and scale-out-only default fallback.

Compared full implementation unit with current App Service overview and authentication docs. Avoided asserting every language runs on every OS or that platform authentication supplies complete business authorization.
Compared complete create-app unit and current configuration docs, including app-setting restart behavior. Keeps Always On requirements and supported runtime combinations qualified.
Compared complete deployment unit with current Deployment Center docs. Original release scenario; no stale assertion that FTP is an automated repository source.

Compared full slot-creation unit with current staging documentation. Includes resource sharing and documented Linux/container auto-swap limitation; avoids guaranteed zero-downtime or database rollback claims.
Compared complete add-slots unit with current clone/swap tables. Default slot-specific behavior is qualified; no claim that cloned settings copy content or private endpoints.
Compared entire security unit with current authentication architecture and rejection choices. Distinguishes authentication from app-specific authorization; qualifies Windows failed-request traces.
Compared full custom-domain unit with current mapping tutorial. Includes TXT verification guidance and supported managed-certificate tiers; avoids unsupported root-CNAME instructions.

Compared full backup unit with current backup documentation. Preserves automatic/custom distinction, virtual-network firewall support, database limitations and verified 31 March 2028 deprecation date.

Compared entire Application Insights unit and current overview. Keeps instrumentation and platform support conditional; original dependency investigation scenario, no promise of automatic universal telemetry.
Compared complete exercise objectives and current hosting/slots/profile docs. Avoids obsolete implication that the PHP target must use Windows; no Azure resources were deployed.
Compared full container/VM comparison with current ACI and Container Apps overview. Qualifies process isolation rather than claiming ACI lacks a VM-equivalent isolation boundary.
Compared full ACI unit and current resource update, groups and Files-mount docs. Preserves deletion/recreation for resource changes and Linux-only feature restrictions.
Compared complete group unit and current group docs. Retains Linux-only multiple containers, shared port namespace, request aggregation and released endpoints.

Compared full Container Apps unit/current overview and scaling docs. Keeps scale-to-zero conditional, explains missing-ingress/custom-rule restart limitation and supported minimum replica baseline; no direct Kubernetes API exposure.
Compared complete exercise objectives with current ACI/group/update documentation. Does not invent the external lab’s image, credentials or command syntax; no resources were deployed.
